home.answerTitle: What is a Minecraft circle generator?
home.answer1: A Minecraft circle generator is a free online tool that turns any diameter into a block-by-block pixel blueprint you can copy directly into the game. Pick a size from 5 to 256 blocks, choose a shape, and the generator draws the exact grid - every row, every block - for circles, ovals, spheres, domes and arcs in both Java and Bedrock editions.
home.answer2: The circle generator uses the same discrete-circle math as the midpoint circle algorithm, which is why odd diameters produce a clean, symmetric ring every time. No downloads, no accounts, and the blueprint is always free.
home.sourcesIntro: The circle generator is based on standard discrete-circle rendering, documented by the following public references:
howTo: Choose a shape and a size - odd numbers give a true center block.
Copy the blueprint block by block, or use Builder mode to step through every placement.
Export a PNG, SVG or copy /setblock commands with your world coordinates.
For spheres, domes, toruses and ellipsoids, build one layer at a time from the bottom up.

items.q: How do I build a circle in Minecraft?
items.a: Pick a diameter, copy the blueprint from the grid, then place the blocks one by one. Start at the center block and work outward for a perfect result every time.

items.q: What circle size should I use?
items.a: Small circles (5-15 blocks) suit fountains and windows, 21-49 is right for towers and rooms, and anything above 65 is for huge builds like stadiums and coliseums.

items.q: Do the blueprints work for Java and Bedrock?
items.a: Yes. The grid shows block positions, so it works identically in Java Edition and Bedrock Edition.

items.q: How do I build a sphere or dome?
items.a: Switch to the sphere or dome tab, then use the Layer slider to see each slice from bottom to top. Build one layer at a time and the shape assembles itself.
